newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Serbs again snub international community.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serbs again snub international community.

text.p: Bosnian Serbs snubbed the international community again on Saturday, rebuffing high-level efforts to persuade them to cooperate with post-war democratic institutions in the former Yugoslav republic.

Momcilo Krajisnik, the Serb member of Bosnia's three-man presidency, made his first visit to central Sarajevo since his forces ended their siege of the capital for talks with German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and U.S. envoy John Kornblum.
Kinkel described the talks at the German embassy as a step forward but said the hardline Serb leader had not reversed his refusal to sign a declaration of loyalty to Bosnian statehood.
Krajisnik and Serb deputies infuriated the international community last week when they boycotted the opening of Bosnia's multi-ethnic parliament and refused to swear the oath to Bosnian statehood.
Kinkel told a news conference that efforts to persuade Krajisnik to change his mind had foundered over the choice of venue for a signing.
"I would have liked there to have been a signing," he said. "We have not yet reached that point but we have taken a few steps forward."

Kinkel said he told Krajisnik the international community had difficulty in understanding the failure of the Bosnian factions to cooperate. "Those who refuse are isolating themselves and must be ready to take the consequences," he said.

The Bosnian Serbs have been told that they risk losing their share of reconstruction aid if they still refuse to cooperate in the political process following September's elections for the presidency and parliament.

Krajisnik told the Bosnian Serb news agency: "It must always be borne in mind that I do not have a mandate to permit outvoting (in the presidency) and have an obligation to protect the equality of the Serb Republic. There can be no bargaining on this."
Kinkel said it was essential for the Bosnian presidency, comprising Moslem leader Alija Izetbegovic, Kresimir Zubak, a Croat, and Krajisnik, to meet again soon.
Krajisnik's refusal to sign the oath marked a further setback to the peace process in Bosnia, where the Serbs have threatened to pull out of municipal elections scheduled for November 23 and 24.
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, which is organising the polls, said there was a "substantial risk" that the elections might be delayed.
"There are significant fears that if the current security situation were to continue from now to the municipal elections, they would be put substantially at risk," OSCE spokesman David Foley said.
Postponing the elections would pose a major security headache as NATO is set to begin a rapid withdrawal of its 58,000 peacekeeping troops after the November polls.
